Definition of obsolete generation test and unstable zap detection.
Internals of shadow page preparation, commit, remote flush and yield helpers.
Control, defaults and topology of two dimensional paging enablement and root lifetime.

findings.text: A host interface discards paging state associated with a guest memory slot being deleted, moved or reconfigured, choosing between a full table discard and a precise range discard according to virtual machine type and quirk state.

Range based translation invalidation is available for classic reverse mapped tables and for two dimensional paging tables, reporting whether remote processors need a translation cache flush and requesting a reload when the private interrupt controller slot is affected.

Reclamation of paging structures from superseded generations and completion of a fast full discard for invalidated two dimensional roots are provided as separate helpers used around memory slot updates.

Virtual processor lifecycle helpers remove all processors of a virtual machine, release generic processor resources, and tear down architecture specific processor state including paging, emulation context and device models.
Paravirtual and emulated device teardown is exposed through small routines for guest clock, Xen shared state and timers, Hyper-V timers, local interrupt controller and performance counters.
A rate limited diagnostic emitter annotates host messages with the current process identifier, and a lightweight kick requests a target processor to exit guest mode without blocking.
Guest memory extensions are notified of range invalidation through a vendor hook, while a weak default hook for reclaimed guest memory does nothing unless overridden by an architecture.
Queued paging structures are maintained in creation order so encountering the first structure still belonging to the current generation proves no older obsolete structures remain later in the walk.

Memory slot changes operate on a detached copy that is marked invalid and installed before activation, after which no new translations may reference the old location and validation is delegated to frame lookup and visibility checks.

Translation invalidation for a frame interval consults reverse maps when present and two dimensional tables when enabled, always including invalidated roots and mapping privacy filters to direct versus mirrored root sets.

Two dimensional paging walks are bounded above by one past the maximum host addressable frame, and mirrored paging is reported only for a specific confidential virtual machine type, otherwise only direct roots are considered.
Leaf clearing skips non present entries and non terminal levels, writes a canonical non present value, and only requests a remote flush when the owning root remains valid.
A validity filtered iterator selects only paging structures whose frame matches the query and that shadow guest entries, built on a hash lookup for that frame.
Remote cache maintenance commits queued invalidations when any exist and otherwise issues a pure remote flush, returning whether any action was taken, with a no work case doing nothing.
Overlap detection scans slots intersecting a frame interval and reports a conflict only when a different slot identifier is encountered.
Processor lookup validates the index against the current online count, clamps speculation, orders against creation, and only then loads from the processor array.
Error frame numbers are recognized by testing a dedicated mask bit, and unmapping distinguishes error values, ordinary mapped pages and memory mapped input output regions.
Disabled builds provide empty destroy helpers and a timer enable check that always reports false, allowing common teardown paths to remain unconditional.

When Xen timer support is present, enablement reflects whether a virtual interrupt is assigned, stopping cancels the host timer and clears expiry and pending counts, and Hyper-V timer release similarly cancels and clears pending indications.
A Hyper-V synthetic timer can recover its owning processor by stepping back by its index to the array base and then obtaining the enclosing control block.

Obsolete reclamation and fast discard completion require the slot mutex to be held, with completion additionally requiring that the paging write lock is not held, while slot flush and leaf clearing require the paging lock in write mode.

Range invalidation requires either an invalidation epoch in progress or the slot lock, root iteration asserts the paging lock and filters by address space, and mirror root release during processor teardown takes the paging lock for reading.

Cached frame deactivation serializes refresh with a mutex, mutates active state under an interrupt safe write lock, and protects global list membership with a separate spin lock, preserving address translation while dropping mapping.
Slot invalidation releases and reacquires the architecture slot mutex around activation and copies fresh architecture data back, relying on writers to look up slots only after acquiring that mutex.

A memory slot duplicate preserves base_gfn, npages, userspace_addr, dirty_bitmap, arch, flags, id and as_id, enabling an invalidated version to substitute for the live entry without losing descriptive state.
A range descriptor carries slot, start, end, may_block and attr_filter, identifying the affected slot interval, blocking permission and privacy selection for invalidation.

Slot creation installs and activates a new entry, deletion removes from inactive and clears the invalidated active entry, relocation replaces inactive then swaps invalidated active for the new location, and flag updates replace in both sets without intermediate invalidation.

A frame cache transitions from active and valid to inactive and invalid under lock, detaches from the global list, and releases prior mapping, leaving address translation cached for later revalidation.

Processor teardown progresses through completion queue drain, paging unload, time and device detachment, vendor release and final freeing of generic resources, with array removal and online count reset at the virtual machine level.
Obsolete and slot page zapping proceeds in bounded batches, yielding the paging lock on contention and restarting the walk, with unstable transitions also restarting to preserve consistency.

Slot driven paging invalidation enters through a slot flush routine invoked after a slot is marked invalid and activated, which then fans out to guest memory, reverse map and two dimensional handlers.
Virtual machine teardown enters via a routine that iterates all processors, destroys each, verifies removal from visibility, and resets the online count.
An invalid paging structure unexpectedly remaining on the active queue is skipped with a one time warning to avoid an endless rescan loop.

Deferring clearing of invalidated two dimensional roots past slot deletion would leave translations unreachable to later callbacks and risk use after free, so they are emptied synchronously before return.

Paging structures that shadow guest entries must be released before the slot disappears because accounting lives in slot memory, and freed tables require a remote kick beforehand to exclude concurrent lockless walks.
Destroying processors can trigger virtual machine wide requests, so removal asserts that neither array load nor indexed lookup can still observe the departing processor.
KVM_MEMSLOT_INVALID tags a slot undergoing deletion or relocation, while KVM_FILTER_PRIVATE and KVM_FILTER_SHARED select which paging root sets participate in range handling.

KVM_X86_DEFAULT_VM combined with KVM_X86_QUIRK_SLOT_ZAP_ALL selects full discard, APIC_ACCESS_PAGE_PRIVATE_MEMSLOT identifies the private interrupt page slot, and KVM_REQ_APIC_PAGE_RELOAD requests its reload.

KVM_DIRECT_ROOTS, KVM_MIRROR_ROOTS and KVM_INVALID_ROOTS classify paging roots, KVM_X86_TDX_VM denotes the mirrored type, and KVM_PFN_ERR_FAULT with KVM_PFN_ERR_NOSLOT_MASK encode erroneous frame cache values.
SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE denotes a cleared entry, PG_LEVEL_4K is the smallest walk level, and KVM_MAX_HUGEPAGE_LEVEL bounds reverse map huge page handling.
Paging teardown releases five dedicated object caches and frees pae_root, pml4_root and pml5_root, restoring encryption treatment on the legacy root when two dimensional paging is disabled.
Xen virtual machine release deactivates shinfo_cache, frees channel records in evtchn_ports, destroys that table, and drops the global enable reference when a configuration flag required it.
Local interrupt controller release cancels its timer, adjusts global keys tracking absent or disabled controllers, and frees register storage and the controller block.
Xen processor release stops the virtual timer when enabled, deactivates runstate and time caches, and synchronously deletes the polling timer.
